title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 302: Rewiring the Self: Neuroplasticity
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 302 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Rewiring the Self: The Nuances of Neuroplasticity

Paragraph 1. For a long time, doctors believed that an adult human brain could never change. Medical books taught that after early childhood, the brain became hard and fixed like concrete. If a person lost a skill after an accident, people thought it was gone forever. However, over the last thirty years, scientists discovered 'neuroplasticity'. This means the brain can always build new paths when we learn.

Paragraph 2. In the late 1970s, scientist Michael Merzenich studied touch in monkeys. When one finger stopped sending signals, nearby brain areas quickly took over that empty space. Later, researcher Eleanor Maguire scanned the brains of London taxi drivers. Because they spent years memorizing 25,000 streets, the map-learning part of their brains grew visibly larger.

Paragraph 3. Sadly, many popular books make false promises about brain change. They claim anyone can learn languages overnight or cure sadness easily using phone apps. Scientist Dr. Hannah West warns against this false hope. She explains a 'paradox': because repeated practice makes brain paths stronger, bad habits like drug addiction and worry loops grow stronger too.

Paragraph 4. Dr. West reminds us that real brain change needs high body energy and long, careful practice. Ten minutes of playing easy puzzle games on a mobile phone cannot rebuild your brain. Real medical training helps patients slowly, unlike quick commercial promises.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions:
Complete the notes below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
groups.template:
• Old textbooks said the adult brain grew fixed like hard 1. {{q1}} .
  • Michael Merzenich discovered new brain paths while studying touch in 2. {{q2}} .
  • Eleanor Maguire found larger map-learning areas in London taxi 3. {{q3}} .
  • Short mobile puzzle 4. {{q4}} cannot cause major physical changes in the brain.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...scanned the brains of London taxi drivers."
Đoạn 4: "...playing easy puzzle games on a mobile phone..."

q5.text: What did doctors believe about adult brains in the past?
options: A. They grew bigger every single month.
B. They worked faster than child brains.
C. They could never change or fix themselves.
D. They could only change through phone apps.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bác sĩ từng tin não người lớn không bao giờ thay đổi được (could never change).

q6.text: What happened in Michael Merzenich's animal experiment?
options: A. Nearby brain areas took over an unused space.
B. The monkeys forgot how to climb trees.
C. The animals learned to read city street maps.
D. Brain cells stopped working completely.

steps: Đoạn 2: Các vùng não lân cận chiếm lấy khoảng trống không còn nhận tín hiệu.

q7.text: Why does Dr. Hannah West describe a brain 'paradox'?
options: A. Because older people always have stronger memories
B. Because mobile games are very expensive to buy
C. Because language learning harms eye vision
D. Because repetition can build bad habits as easily as good ones

steps: Đoạn 3: Lặp lại khiến cả thói quen xấu lẫn tốt đều mạnh lên.

q8.text: According to Dr. West, what does real brain change require?
options: A. Eating more sweet food before sleeping
B. Strong energy and long, careful practice
C. Ten minutes of easy smartphone puzzles
D. Living alone without talking to anyone

steps: Đoạn 4: "...needs high body energy and long, careful practice."
